who: Factory B builders, reviewers, CI jobs, and receiving implementation agents
what: A deterministic verifier for package manifest, hash, file-count, path, and regular-file integrity
why: Every reusable Factory package needs a cheap independent byte/path integrity check before semantic verification or release review
when: After package creation, after transport/read-back, and before higher-level evidence or release decisions
where: Local Linux, GitHub Actions, or another environment with Python 3.11+
how: Read root MANIFEST.json, validate declared rows, compare bytes/sizes/paths, reject unsafe entries, and emit a JSON receipt
inputs: Factory package directory or ZIP containing root MANIFEST.json
constraints: No extraction of ZIP content is required
approval_boundary: The verifier may report byte/path integrity only; external release still requires the governing Release Contract and scoped approval
recovery: Rebuild the package from the frozen source candidate and regenerate the manifest
known_limitations: v1 supports the current Factory B MANIFEST.json shape
It proves integrity, not semantic quality or provenance truth
